title: Unified Multi-Provider SDK Patterns
summary: For intermediate developers, this module teaches you to build and test a thin adapter over the native Anthropic, OpenAI, and Google SDKs. After completing it, you can normalize provider response shapes, stop signals, usage, and storage behavior without assuming that different compatibility endpoints drop the same guarantees.
objectives: Map the native request and response shapes of the Claude Messages API, the OpenAI Responses API, and the Gemini generateContent and Interactions APIs onto one internal contract.
Normalize stop signals and token usage so that truncation, refusal, pauses, and tool requests are never mistaken for a completed answer.
Distinguish Anthropic's documented OpenAI compatibility limitations from Google's different documented compatibility behavior and decide when a compatibility layer is acceptable.
Keep model identifiers, API surface, and conversation-storage policy in configuration that a contract test verifies against the provider's documentation.

sections.title: Three SDKs, three different ideas of a response
paragraphs: A portable client starts by admitting that the providers do not agree on what a response is. The Claude Messages API takes the system prompt as a top-level `system` parameter and prior turns in a `messages` array, and returns an assistant message whose `content` is an array of typed blocks such as `text` and `tool_use`. Anthropic describes the Messages API as usable for single queries or stateless multi-turn conversations: your application resends whatever history the model should see.

The OpenAI Responses API, which OpenAI recommends for new projects while Chat Completions remains supported, returns an `output` array of Items. A `message` is one Item type; `reasoning`, `function_call`, and `function_call_output` are others, and OpenAI's migration guide lists treating every output entry as a message as a common error. The SDK's `output_text` helper joins the text for you, but only the Items tell you what else happened. Responses are stored by default unless you send `store: false`.

Google documents two Gemini surfaces. `generateContent` returns `candidates`, each with `content.parts` and a `finishReason`. The Interactions API returns an Interaction with a `status` and a `steps` timeline containing entries such as `user_input`, `function_call`, and `model_output`. Google's Interactions overview recommends it for new projects and calls `generateContent` legacy but still supported. An adapter lets you make that choice once, in one place, and reverse it later without touching every caller.
sections.callout: The SDK is not the abstraction. The abstraction is the internal contract you write; each SDK sits behind an adapter that fills it.

sections.title: Normalize stop signals before you normalize text
paragraphs: The most expensive portability bug is a truncated or refused answer that flows downstream as if it were complete. Each provider signals this differently. Claude sets `stop_reason` to a documented value such as `end_turn`, `max_tokens`, `stop_sequence`, `tool_use`, `pause_turn`, `refusal`, or `model_context_window_exceeded`. The Responses API marks a cut-off answer with `status: "incomplete"` and can provide an `incomplete_details.reason` such as `max_output_tokens`; a safety refusal appears as a `refusal` content item instead of ordinary text. Gemini's `generateContent` reports a `finishReason`, with `STOP` indicating a normal finish, and an Interaction waiting on a function result has `status: "requires_action"`.

Map every native value into your own outcome, and make the mapping total: an unknown value becomes `other` and fails closed; it never defaults to `complete`. Keep the raw value as well, because it is needed to investigate why a response stopped. `pause_turn` deserves its own outcome: Anthropic documents it as a paused long-running turn that can be sent back to let the model continue, which is neither success nor failure.

Usage needs the same treatment. Field names differ: `usage.input_tokens` and `output_tokens` on Claude and OpenAI Responses, and `usageMetadata.promptTokenCount` and `candidatesTokenCount` on Gemini `generateContent`. Their accounting also differs. Anthropic notes that its counts do not match visible content one-to-one and that total input includes `input_tokens`, `cache_creation_input_tokens`, and `cache_read_input_tokens`. OpenAI notes that chaining with `previous_response_id` still bills earlier input tokens. Store raw usage beside any normalized figure so a cost comparison can be audited.

Streaming multiplies the differences. Responses streaming emits typed server-sent events such as `response.output_text.delta`, `response.function_call_arguments.delta`, and `response.completed`; Gemini can stream structured output as partial JSON strings that must be concatenated; Claude's `stop_reason` is null in the `message_start` event and set later in the stream. A streaming adapter should emit the same internal events whatever the source, and declare an outcome only after the final stop signal arrives.

sections.title: OpenAI-compatible endpoints are a test harness, not an abstraction
paragraphs: Both Anthropic and Google let the official OpenAI SDK talk to their models by changing the connection details and model name. That can look like a unified client, but the two compatibility endpoints do not document identical behavior. Read each provider's limitations before using either route.

Anthropic states that its compatibility layer is primarily intended to test and compare model capabilities and is not considered a long-term or production-ready solution for most use cases. On that layer the `strict` flag on function tools is ignored, so tool arguments are not guaranteed to follow your schema; `response_format` is ignored; `n` must be 1; `temperature` above 1 is capped at 1; system and developer messages are hoisted and concatenated into one leading system message; `choices[].message.refusal` is always empty; and prompt caching is unavailable. Anthropic also says unsupported fields are generally ignored rather than rejected.

Google documents different behavior for its OpenAI compatibility route. It maps `reasoning_effort` onto Gemini thinking settings, exposes Gemini-specific features through `extra_body`, and documents ignored parameters in its image-generation compatibility behavior. Google recommends calling the Gemini API directly if you are not already using the OpenAI libraries. The supplied Google material does not establish that Gemini compatibility ignores `strict` tool schemas or `response_format`, so this module does not attribute those Anthropic-specific limitations to Google.

The failure mode on Anthropic's route is quiet. A request that relies on `strict` or `response_format` can still succeed at the protocol level even though the field is ignored, so a malformed argument or incorrectly shaped answer can reach production. Use the compatibility routes only for behavior their respective documentation supports. If you retain one, write a contract test for every guarantee your application needs rather than assuming that Anthropic and Google drop the same features.

Update note for 2026-09-18: the source URLs and their 2026-09-13 verification dates remain within the 30-day review cadence. This correction changes the earlier narration and transcript, which incorrectly said both Claude and Gemini compatibility endpoints silently ignore `strict` tool schemas and `response_format`. Those specific limitations are now attributed only to Anthropic; Google's separately documented behavior remains unchanged.
sections.callout: Compatibility is provider-specific. A limitation documented for Anthropic must not be copied to Google's route without Google documentation that supports it.

code.label: Guarantees are tests, not assumptions

sections.title: Model ids, API surface, and storage policy belong in configuration
paragraphs: Model identifiers and available capabilities can change faster than application code. Put each identifier in configuration, record where and when it was verified, and fail startup or continuous integration when it is missing. Never let an adapter fall back to a hardcoded default that nobody reviews. Anthropic's Models API can provide model metadata that a startup check can inspect.

Documentation can change, which is why the check belongs in code. Provider surfaces and lifecycle labels can drift after a design decision is recorded. A contract test that makes one real call per configured surface-and-model pair establishes whether that pair works for your project on the day you deploy; a source-code comment does not.

Treat state and retention as configuration too, because the defaults differ. The Claude Messages API expects your application to resend the history the model should see. The Responses API stores responses unless you send `store: false`. The Gemini Interactions API stores interactions by default; setting `store=false` disables `previous_interaction_id` chaining, and interaction-scoped settings must be resent when chaining. A unified client that exposes one `store` switch has to translate it per surface and reject a combination the surface cannot honor rather than quietly retaining data contrary to policy.

code.label: Routes are data with provenance

activity.title: Build and probe a three-provider adapter
instructions: Define an internal result contract with outcome, joined text, tool calls with ids, raw stop value, and raw usage. Write one adapter each for Claude Messages, OpenAI Responses, and one Gemini surface. State in one paragraph why you chose generateContent or Interactions for Gemini.
Write a total stop-signal mapping for each adapter and a unit test that feeds it every documented value plus one invented value. The invented value must not map to complete.

In a test environment, point the OpenAI SDK at Anthropic's compatibility endpoint and send one request that depends on strict tool arguments and one that depends on response_format. Record what the layer did with each. Do not infer that Google's compatibility endpoint behaves the same way.

Move every model id and storage setting into configuration with a verified-on date and source URL, and add a contract test that fails the build when a configured id is rejected or a storage setting cannot be honored on its surface.
evidence: Adapter code or a design, plus the stop-signal mapping table and its tests, including the invented-value case.

A short compatibility-layer finding that separates Anthropic's documented dropped guarantees from Google's separately documented compatibility behavior and names native features only where the source establishes them.
A configuration file listing model ids, surfaces, and storage settings, each with a verified-on date and the URL it was verified against.
activity.reflectionPrompt: Which provider difference would your adapter have hidden from you if you had normalized the text first and the stop signals second?

questions.prompt: A Claude response comes back with stop_reason "max_tokens". What should a portable adapter report?
choices: Complete, because text was returned
Truncated, because the output reached a token limit and may be incomplete
Refused
A tool request
questions.explanation: "max_tokens" indicates that generation reached a token limit, so the returned text may be partial. The adapter must report `truncated` rather than `complete`.

questions.prompt: You call Claude through Anthropic's OpenAI SDK compatibility endpoint with a function tool marked strict: true. What does Anthropic document about that flag?
choices: It is enforced exactly as it is on OpenAI
It is ignored, so tool arguments are not guaranteed to match the schema
It always returns a 400 error
It reroutes the request to the native Messages API
questions.explanation: Anthropic documents that its compatibility layer ignores `strict`. Code that requires schema-conforming tool arguments must not assume this route preserves that guarantee.

questions.prompt: Why is treating every item in response.output as a message a bug in an OpenAI Responses adapter?
choices: The output array only ever contains one item
Reasoning, function_call, and other Items are distinct types; a message is only one Item type
Messages are returned in a separate choices field
Items are only returned when streaming
questions.explanation: The Responses output is a typed collection. Reasoning and function-call Items must be handled according to their own types rather than parsed as assistant messages.

questions.prompt: Your policy forbids server-side conversation storage features. Which statement about the default behavior is accurate?
choices: All three APIs keep nothing server-side by default
OpenAI Responses and Gemini Interactions store by default and need store set to false; Claude Messages relies on the history the application resends
Only Claude stores conversations by default
Storage is controlled only by the model id
questions.explanation: Responses and Interactions document storage by default with a `store` control, while a Messages conversation is formed from the history the application sends.

questions.prompt: Google's Interactions overview recommends Interactions for new projects and describes generateContent as legacy but supported. What should the adapter designer do?
choices: Assume generateContent has already been removed
Make the surface a configuration choice behind one internal contract, record the reason, and test the chosen surface
Use an OpenAI compatibility endpoint without testing it
Hardcode generateContent in every caller
questions.explanation: Keeping the surface behind an adapter makes the decision reversible. A contract test then checks that the configured surface still behaves as the application requires.

questions.prompt: Which compatibility claim does this module support?
choices: Anthropic and Google both document that strict tool schemas and response_format are ignored
Anthropic documents that strict and response_format are ignored, while the supplied Google material documents different compatibility behavior
Google documents that every unsupported field returns an error
All compatibility endpoints preserve identical guarantees
questions.explanation: The module attributes ignored `strict` and `response_format` fields only to Anthropic. Google's material describes other mappings and limitations, so identical behavior must not be assumed.
